DK92.1 is a medical diagnosis code specifically designating melena (black, tarry stools associated with upper gastrointestinal bleeding) [^src1]. Within the Danish healthcare system's clinical quality databases, this code is a critical component for tracking severe bleeding incidents among patients diagnosed with [[atrieflimren]] (atrial fibrillation) [^src1].

The code is part of a comprehensive set of diagnostic markers used to calculate the incidence of severe bleeding in this patient population [^src1]. Specifically, DK92.1 is categorized alongside other gastrointestinal bleeding codes, such as [[dk92-0|DK92.0]] and [[dk92-2|DK92.2]], as well as codes for intracranial bleeding (ranging from [[di60|DI60]] to [[ds066|DS066]]) and urinary or respiratory bleeding (including [[dj942|DJ942]], [[dn02|DN02]], [[dr04|DR04]], and [[dr31|DR31]]) [^src1]. 

This standardized coding framework is detailed in the annual reports for the Atrial Fibrillation Database in Denmark, published by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) [^src1] [^src2]. By capturing specific events like melena through DK92.1, the database enables standardized data collection and regional comparisons, ultimately supporting the clinical quality measurement and safety monitoring of treatments for atrial fibrillation patients [^src1] [^src2].
